Several papers connect LLMs or learned logic rules to causal reasoning in time series. For extracting verifiable symbolic causal rules with temporal operators and delays from multivariate time-series inputs, ruleXplain uses an LLM with a constrained rule language plus a simulator to generate counterfactual trajectories for candidate explanations [1]. For causal discovery that includes logical/stepwise querying with explicit judgments and confidence, Tree-Query proposes a multi-agent, tree-structured LLM framework to reduce causal discovery to short sequences of queries, aiming for interpretable causal conclusions [3]. For learning causal mechanisms under interventions in time series, SVAR-FM uses a physics-based simulator as a do-operator via variable clamping and then learns interventional conditionals [8].

If your focus is causality-aware time-series forecasting rather than explicit logical rules, CVAformer targets confounding from dynamic components by variable-level disentanglement and causal intervention during alignment [2]. If you need “logical constraints” as a verifier for LLM reasoning (not necessarily time-series causality), PCRLLM constrains LLM inference to single-step logical forms for verifiability [9], and LOVER enforces logical consistency constraints to regularize a verifier [10].
